title: Consolidated Transport Migration Roadmap and Non-blocking Client Rewrite Playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: PRD-level plan to retire the legacy transport surface (multiplexed long-poll + chunked SSE + legacy socket aliases) by introducing a Consolidated Streaming Gateway and a non-blocking client rewrite path. Goal: minimize customer outages during migration, provide automated client adapters and telemetry gates, and ensure rollback-safe phased cutovers. This ticket captures requirements, acceptance criteria, a detailed migration playbook, comms, and success gates.
acceptance_criteria: Consolidated Streaming Gateway (CSG) deployed to sandbox and staging with compatibility adapter responding to legacy multiplexed long-poll and chunked SSE formats
Automated client-adapter CLI that rewrites common SDK usage patterns and emits a compatibility header is built and validated against top 25 customer SDK samples
Telemetry dashboard showing per-route fallback rates, error-class breakdown, and 95th/99th latency for both legacy and unified endpoints available in Console
Canary traffic (1% -> 10% -> 50%) cutover plan executed with automatic rollback on predefined SLO violations
Customer communication templates and migration playbook published with documented mitigation paths and 60-day guaranteed grace period from first notice
All major customers with high-usage or compliance constraints have migration plans or dedicated engineering contacts assigned
migration_steps: Phase 0 - Prep: Inventory top 200 customers using legacy transports, capture SDK versions and known custom integrations
Phase 1 - Adapter Beta: Build and ship server-side compatibility adapters in sandbox and staging; publish client-adapter CLI v0.1
Phase 2 - Shadowing: Enable passive shadowing in production for upgraded SDKs and adapters; collect telemetry for 2 weeks
Phase 3 - Canary: Route 1% traffic for 72h, validate metrics; expand to 10% then 50% as stability gates pass
Phase 4 - Opt-in Grace: Announce opt-in deprecation window and allow customers to opt for extended grace periods (30/60/90 days) via support ticket
Phase 5 - Forced Migration: After grace windows and targeted outreach, retire legacy transport with 7-day final notice for non-responsive customers
timeline: 2025-04-07: Shadowing begins in production for low-risk customers
2025-05-12: Expanded canary to 50% pending gate pass
2025-06-16: Opt-in grace period ends for initial cohort
2025-06-30: Scheduled enforcement date for legacy transport retirement (soft enforcement)
communication_plan: Pre-announcement blog + release notes 45 days before enforcement
Targeted emails to top 200 customers with migration contact and remediation checklist 30 days before enforcement
In-console banner and migration center with automated compatibility checker and link to client-adapter CLI
Weekly migration digest to customers in migration cohort and internal stakeholders
Support playbook for Tier 1/2 with runbooks and escalation matrix
telemetry_and_gates: Gate A (Safety): <1% increase in 95th latency and <0.5% increase in error-rate during 72h 1% canary
Gate B (Stability): <2% fallback-to-legacy rate after 2 weeks of shadowing for canary customers
Gate C (Customer): No P1 incidents attributable to transport change from customers in canary cohort for 14 days
Telemetry: per-tenant fallback_rate, transport_error_codes, socket_reconnects, avg_token_latency, per-route qps
Automated rollback trigger: any gate breaching triggers immediate traffic reversion and paging of on-call engineers
rollout_strategy: Staged: sandbox -> staging -> shadow in prod -> 1% canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full
Customer cohorts: low-risk (self-serve SDKs), medium-risk (custom SDK versions), high-risk (enterprise+compliance) with dedicated timelines
Fallbacks: automatic model-routing to compatible endpoint variants if adapter fails; per-tenant circuit-breaker
Safety nets: extended grace for enterprise customers, temporary compatibility-mode flag for support to toggle
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Silent client integrations break due to custom long-polling logic. Mitigation: run automated static analysis on submitted SDK samples and proactively reach out
Risk: Unexpected surge in fallback/error rates during canary. Mitigation: pre-warm connection pools and enable conservative batching at gateway
Risk: Customer dissatisfaction with enforced migration. Mitigation: offer migration assistance credits and extended grace windows for impacted customers
Risk: Telemetry gaps miss regressions. Mitigation: instrument additional correlation ids and increase retention for migration cohort
